verdict.rationale: Granola documents scheduled transcript auto-deletion with selectable retention periods from 1 day to 1 year. It also lets users permanently remove notes on demand, which covers the core retention and erasure mechanics. However, the retention setting applies only to transcripts, and nothing shows it as an admin-enforced, workspace-wide policy. Missing for 10: evidence that IT admins can set retention centrally for the whole workspace, retention coverage for notes and recordings/audio (transcripts only), documented guarantees of permanent erasure at the workspace or bulk level, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can set retention policies — auto-delete transcripts and recordings on a schedule — and permanently erase data on demand

citations.quote: Granola allows you to automatically delete transcripts after a set period of time. This applies only to transcripts — your notes are not affected and will remain available.
Choose a retention period from the dropdown: 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, or 1 year
Permanently remove notes or recover accidentally deleted ones.
